name: Dubai
tagline: Dubai's first three-Michelin-star restaurant, and the Persian kebab where chefs eat on their days off.

Trèsind Studio.description: Modern Indian cuisine in DIFC, Dubai's first restaurant to earn three Michelin stars.

Al Ustad Special Kabab.description: Persian kebabs in Bur Dubai since 1978, a favorite of the city's chefs on their days off.

Al Mallah.description: Classic Lebanese shawarma for almost 40 years.

Ravi Restaurant.description: A Pakistani food landmark in Al Satwa since 1978, once certified by Anthony Bourdain.

STAY by Yannick Alléno.description: Contemporary French cuisine inside the One&Only The Palm, with a dining room of black crystal chandeliers. Two Michelin stars, reviewed by critic Saeed Saeed for The National.

Hakkasan Dubai.description: London-born Cantonese fine-dining group; its Atlantis The Palm outpost holds one Michelin star in the Dubai guide.

Ossiano.description: Underwater restaurant at Atlantis The Palm overlooking the 65,000-creature Ambassador Lagoon aquarium; one Michelin star for its seafood tasting menu.

Al Muntaha.description: On the 27th floor of the Burj Al Arab, elevated French-Italian cuisine with views over Palm Jumeirah; one Michelin star.

Torno Subito.description: Massimo Bottura's first restaurant outside Italy, at W Dubai - The Palm; playful Italian cooking inspired by his Riviera childhood. One Michelin star.

11 Woodfire.description: Live-fire cooking by chef Akmal Anuar in a converted Jumeirah 1 villa, everything grilled over oak, hickory or hay; one Michelin star.

Smoked Room.description: A 14-seat room by Spanish chef Dani García at St Regis Gardens, Palm Jumeirah, built around fire cooking and smoke; earned a Michelin star just six months after opening.

La Dame de Pic Dubai.description: Anne-Sophie Pic's first Dubai venture, the world's most Michelin-starred female chef, on the 25th floor of One&Only One Za'abeel. One Michelin star.

Orfali Bros Bistro.description: Bistro run by the three Syrian Orfali brothers, playful Mediterranean cooking with global influences; one Michelin star and No. 1 on the 2025 MENA's 50 Best Restaurants list.

3Fils.description: A spot by the Jumeirah Fishing Harbour with a sushi counter and relaxed Asian-inspired cooking over the water; Michelin Bib Gourmand distinction.

Bait Maryam.description: Home-style Levantine cooking by chef Salam Dakkak in Jumeirah Lake Towers, dedicated to her mother Maryam; Michelin Bib Gourmand distinction.

Al Khayma Heritage Restaurant.description: A restaurant-museum in the historic Al Fahidi district serving traditional Emirati dishes like machboos in a courtyard with live music; Michelin Bib Gourmand distinction.

Kinoya.description: A Japanese ramen and izakaya counter on Sheikh Zayed Road, named the UAE's best restaurant on the MENA's 50 Best list; Michelin Bib Gourmand distinction.

Reif Japanese Kushiyaki.description: Specialists in kushiyaki, grilled Japanese skewers, with a second branch in Dubai Hills; Michelin Bib Gourmand distinction.

Berenjak Dubai.description: An outpost of the London Persian kababi at Dar Wasl Mall, with charcoal-grilled kebabs and mezze at accessible prices; Michelin Bib Gourmand distinction.

Ibn AlBahr.description: A fisherman-owned Lebanese seafood restaurant by the Dubai Creek Golf & Yacht Club; Michelin Bib Gourmand distinction.

Bu Qtair.description: A no-frills fish shack in Umm Suqeim where you pick your fresh catch and it's fried on the spot; visited by Anthony Bourdain in his Dubai special.

Al Fanar Restaurant & Cafe.description: A heritage Emirati restaurant group; its outpost at Al Seef Heritage Village on Dubai Creek recreates 1950s Dubai. Featured in the Michelin Guide Dubai.

Aroos Damascus.description: A decades-old Syrian institution in the heart of Deira, its façade taking up almost an entire block of Al Muraqqabat Road.

Karachi Darbar.description: A family-run Pakistani chain in Al Karama since 1973, known for its tikkas, biryanis and karahis at wallet-friendly prices.

Saravanaa Bhavan.description: An outpost of the South Indian vegetarian chain founded in 1981, a go-to for dosas and idlis in the Karama neighborhood.

Arabian Tea House.description: A café set in a restored pearl trader's house in the historic Al Fahidi (Bastakiya) district, serving Arabic tea and traditional breakfasts in a courtyard beneath wind towers.

Ashwaq Cafeteria.description: An unpretentious shawarma stall a few blocks from the Deira Gold Souk, recommended by Lonely Planet for its chicken shawarma and fresh juices.

Zaroob.description: A 24-hour Levantine street-food chain born in Dubai in 2010; known for its fateer and late-night shawarma.

XVA Café.description: A vegetarian café inside the XVA Art Hotel, a traditional windtower house turned art gallery in the heart of Bastakiya.

Zuma Dubai.description: An outpost of the London-born contemporary Japanese group, with a robata grill and izakaya-style dining in DIFC; one of the city's hardest tables to book.

La Petite Maison Dubai.description: The DIFC Gate Village outpost of the French-Mediterranean LPM group, famous for its tarte fine and high-profile clientele.

Nobu Dubai.description: On the 22nd floor of Atlantis The Palm; Nobu Matsuhisa's Japanese-Peruvian cuisine with views over Palm Jumeirah.

Pierchic.description: At the end of a private pier at Madinat Jumeirah, with views of the Burj Al Arab; specializing in seafood and Mediterranean cuisine.

Pai Thai.description: A Thai restaurant reached by traditional abra boat through the canals of Madinat Jumeirah; named Time Out Dubai's best Southeast Asian restaurant several years running.

Salt.description: A gourmet-burger food truck launched in 2014 that popularized the #FindSalt social-media treasure hunt; now permanently parked at Kite Beach.

Ninive.description: A Middle Eastern restaurant styled like an Arabian tent by the Emirates Towers, known for its tamarind chicken and lobster tagine.

COYA Dubai.description: An outpost of the London-born Peruvian group, at the Four Seasons on Jumeirah Beach, with ceviches, pisco sours and a party atmosphere.

Logma.description: A chain reinventing Emirati street and childhood food, like jareesh or luqaimat, in a casual format inside The Dubai Mall.

Calicut Paragon.description: An outpost of the group founded in Calicut, Kerala, in 1939; a go-to for South Indian cooking in the Karama neighborhood.

Fix Dessert Chocolatier.description: The Dubai brand that created the pistachio-and-kataifi chocolate bar in 2021, which went globally viral in 2023 after a TikTok video; now also sold at Dubai Airport (Terminal 3).
